commitResults.messageBody:
Rename the main class to Nick and add a greeting message that
introduces the chatbot when it starts up.

Read user commands in a loop and echo each one back. Exit the
loop when the user types the bye command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for add and list
commitResults.messageBody:
Store text entered by the user in a fixed-size array and confirm
each addition with an added message. The list command prints the
stored items in a numbered list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for marking tasks as done
commitResults.messageBody:
Track the done status of each task and add a mark command that
sets a task as done. The list command now shows a status icon
for each task.

Add an unmark command that reverses the done status of a task,
setting it back to not done.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract task data into a Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a separate Task class that holds a description and done
status, and expose methods to mark, unmark, and query it. Replace
the parallel arrays with a single array of Task objects.

commitResults.messageTitle: Comply with SE-EDU Java coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the required Javadoc header comments for the classes and public
methods so the code follows the SE-EDU Java coding standard. No
behaviour changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for todos, deadlines, and events
commitResults.messageBody:
Add three task types tracked with a type field on the Task class:
todos, deadlines (with a by time), and events (with a from and to
time). Update the add confirmation and list output to show the
type icon and any date details. Dates are kept as plain strings
for now.

Introduce Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses of Task, each
overriding the type icon and display format. This replaces the
single Task class that used a type field, so behaviour specific to
each task type now lives in its own class.

Extract a reply helper that wraps output lines between the two
divider lines, and a replyAdded helper for the add confirmation.
Previously every command repeated the divider printing inline,
which was duplicated logic that made the main loop noisy and easy
to get wrong. The command handlers now describe what to say rather
than how to frame it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Encapsulate task storage in a TaskList class
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the fixed-size task array and the running count into a new
TaskList class that exposes add, get, and size. Previously the main
loop managed the array and the count directly, which mixed storage
bookkeeping with command handling and duplicated the count++ logic
across every add branch. The main loop now works with a higher-level
task list abstraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract list rendering into its own method
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the code that builds the numbered task list out of the main
loop into a renderList method. Previously the list command mixed
loop control and array indexing with display formatting inside the
already long main method, making it read at an inconsistent level
of abstraction. The main loop now simply asks for the list lines
and prints them.
